name: Stenbolone
lead: Stenbolone (2-methyl-Δ1-dihydrotestosterone) is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, related to drostanolone and 1-testosterone. Wikipedia states the compound itself was never marketed.[1]

Its 17β-acetate ester, stenbolone acetate, was sold as a depot intramuscular injection under names such as Anatrofin and Stenobolone.[1] A 1969 Mexican paper examined stenbolone acetate's effects on the normal ovary.[2]

Human data are limited to metabolism studies: after a single oral dose of the acetate to a volunteer, researchers identified nine urinary metabolites and detected the parent compound for more than 120 hours.[3] Equine anti-doping work includes it among screened anabolic steroids.[4]

paras: Stenbolone is an androgen receptor agonist.[1] In a human metabolism study, only a small share of the dose (about 6.6 percent) was excreted as the parent compound, with most appearing as metabolites.[3] Further urinary metabolites, including 18-hydroxylated forms, have been isolated.[5]
As an anabolic steroid it is among compounds screened for in racehorse urine and relevant to sport anti-doping.[4] No information on its legal status was found in the sources reviewed.
No studies found on muscle or appearance outcomes. The only human work identified concerns metabolism and one 1969 gynecological study of stenbolone acetate.[2][3][5]

timeline.event: Study of stenbolone acetate's effects on the normal ovary published.[2]
Urinary metabolites of stenbolone acetate characterised in a human volunteer.[3]

card.summary: A DHT-derived anabolic steroid whose acetate ester was an old injectable; known today mostly from metabolism studies.

quick.overview:
Stenbolone is a DHT-derived anabolic steroid. Only its acetate ester was ever sold, as an injectable.

The human literature is thin and mostly concerns metabolism and detection.
quick.mechanism: It acts as an androgen receptor agonist; the acetate ester serves as a depot prodrug.
quick.risks: No clinical safety data were found beyond its classification as an anabolic steroid. Legal status was not documented in the sources reviewed.
